scenes.title: Observability Tooling (Monte Carlo, OpenLineage)
scenes.subtitle: Platforms and standards for data health
scenes.narration: Modern observability relies on platforms like Monte Carlo and open standards like OpenLineage to automate monitoring and share lineage.

scenes.heading: Platform versus open standard
scenes.narration: Monte Carlo is a managed platform that automatically learns baselines and detects anomalies across the five pillars with minimal setup. OpenLineage is instead an open specification that standardizes how tools emit lineage events. One gives you a turnkey product, while the other gives the ecosystem a common language so tools interoperate.

scenes.heading: What these tools provide
bullets: Automated monitoring across the five pillars
Machine-learned baselines instead of manual thresholds
End-to-end lineage stitched from many systems
Alerting and incident workflows out of the box
scenes.narration: Platforms provide automated monitoring so you do not hand-write every check across freshness, volume, schema, distribution, and lineage. They learn baselines with machine learning, reducing the burden of tuning thresholds. They stitch lineage across many systems and ship alerting and incident workflows ready to use.

scenes.heading: An OpenLineage run event
scenes.code:
eventType: COMPLETE
eventTime: '2026-07-07T10:00:00Z'
run:
  runId: 8f1c-abcd-a2
job:
  namespace: analytics
  name: build_orders
inputs:
  - namespace: warehouse
    name: raw.orders
outputs:
  - namespace: warehouse
    name: mart.orders
    facets:
      dataQuality:
        rowCount: 1024
scenes.narration: This OpenLineage event describes a completed run of a job that builds the orders mart. It declares the input and output datasets, which is exactly the information needed to assemble a lineage graph. The dataQuality facet attaches metrics like row count, so quality signals travel alongside lineage in a vendor-neutral format.

scenes.text: Use platforms for turnkey monitoring and open standards like OpenLineage to keep lineage portable across tools.
scenes.narration: Managed platforms accelerate coverage without heavy engineering, while open standards prevent lock-in and unify lineage. The two approaches complement each other in a mature stack.
